{{Short description|French mathematician}}
[[File:CohenAlbert2010 MFO12757.jpg|thumb|Albert Cohen]]
'''Albert Cohen''' (born 29 June 1965 in Paris) is a French mathematician, specializing in [[approximation theory]], [[numerical analysis]], and digital [[signal processing]].

==Biography==
He is, through maternal descent, the grand-nephew of the physicist [[Jacques Solomon]]. From 1984 to 1987 Albert Cohen was a student at the [[École Polytechnique]]. In 1990 he defended his doctoral thesis at [[Paris Dauphine University]]. His thesis, written under the supervision of [[Yves Meyer]], is entitled ''Ondelettes, analyse multi résolution et traitement numérique du signal'' (Wavelets, multiresolution analysis and digital signal analysis)<ref>{{cite thesis|title=''Ondelettes, analyse multi résolution et traitement numérique du signal'' par Albert Cohen|url=https://www.theses.fr/1990PA090018|website=theses.fr|date=January 1990|type=These de doctorat|last1=Cohen|first1=Albert}}</ref> From 1990 to 1991 Cohen was a postdoc at [[Bell Laboratories]] at Murray Hill. He completed his [[habilitation]] in 1992 at Paris Dauphine University. From 1993 to 1995 he worked at [[ENSTA Paris]]. Since 1995 he has been a professor at the ''Laboratoire Jacques-Louis Lions'' of [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris 6),<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=Albert Cohen|website=Laboratoire Jacques-Louis Lions, Université Pierre-et-Marie-Curie|url=https://www.ljll.math.upmc.fr/cohen/}}</ref> which is a component of [[Sorbonne University]]. He is the author of 3 books and the author of co-author of over 100 research articles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Invited Speaker: Albert Cohen, Sorbonne University|website=8th European Mathematical Congress (8EMC)|url=https://8ecm.si/programme/invited-speakers/18}}</ref>

Cohen developed in 1990, with [[Ingrid Daubechies]] and Jean-Christophe Feauveau, the first biorthogonal bases for [[wavelets]];<ref>
{{cite journal
| author1 = Cohen, Albert Cohen | author2 = Daubechies, Ingrid | author3 = Feauveau, Jean-Christophe
| title = Biorthogonal bases of compactly supported wavelets
| journal = Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics
| volume = 45
| number = 5
| date = 1992
| pages = 485–560
| doi = 10.1002/cpa.3160450502 }}</ref> this research has an important application in the image compression standard [[JPEG]]-2000. With [[Wolfgang Dahmen (mathematician)|Wolfgang Dahmen]] and [[Ronald DeVore]], Cohen then worked on the analysis of nonlinear and adaptive approximation methods, with a view to applications in learning theory and in [[numerical analysis]] of [[partial differential equation]]s. He is interested in algorithmic problems involving a very large number of variables, which cause a prohibitive increase in the complexity of calculations. These problems arise in [[statistical learning]] theory, in the treatment of parametric and [[stochastic partial differential equation]]s, and in the development of [[w:Response surface methodology|response surfaces]] from computer software involving adaptive numerical methods.<ref name=homepage/>

In 2000 Cohen received the [[Jacques Herbrand Prize|''grand prix Jacques Herbrand'']] from the [[French Academy of Sciences]]. In 1995 he won the V. A. Popov Prize in approximation theory from the University of South Carolina and in 2004 the ''prix Blaise Pascal'' from the French Academy of Sciences. He was elected in 1998 a junior member and in 2013 a senior member of the ''Institut Universitaire de France''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iufrance.fr/les-membres-de-liuf/membre/50.html|title=Albert Cohen|website=Institut Universitaire de France}}</ref> He was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) in Beijing in 2002,<ref>{{cite book|author=Cohen, Albert|chapter=Adaptive methods for PDE´s: Wavelets or Mesh Refinement?|title=Proceedings of the ICM, Beijing 2002|volume=1|pages=607–620}} [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0212414 arXiv preprint]</ref> a plenary speaker at the [[International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (ICIAM) in Zurich in 2007, and an invited speaker at the conference [[Dynamics, Equations and Applications]] in [[Kraków]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DEA 2019 Invited Speakers |url=https://www.dea.agh.edu.pl/invitedspeakers |access-date=2023-03-17}}</ref>

In 2013 Cohen was awarded an [[European Research Council|ERC]] [[European Research Council#Schemes|Advanced Grant]] for a project called BREAD (''Breaking the curse of dimensionality in analysis and simulation '').
